title: Session coordination fabric
description: Objective: provide daemon-mediated communication among authenticated coder sessions, terminal/effect wrappers, reviewers, and the control room without recreating general chat. Deliverable: a packages/coordination service with typed addressed REQUEST, RESPONSE, EVENT, CONTROL, and HANDOFF envelopes, durable mailboxes, correlation, ordering, dedupe, expiry, backpressure, and replay. NOT in scope: peer-to-peer authority, social channels, arbitrary remote shell, secret forwarding, or treating free-form text as a command. Hard dependencies: Runtime contract registry, Identity session core, and Projection outbox core. Owned paths: packages/coordination/**. Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/coordination typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/coordination test.
definitionOfDone: Every endpoint and envelope is authenticated, capability-scoped, versioned, bounded, addressed, correlated, and durably sequenced.
At-least-once delivery deduplicates; cursor gaps, expiry, overload, unknown recipients, and restart produce typed outcomes without silent loss.
Terminal messages bind an existing effect/session identity; advisory text cannot mutate lifecycle or grant authority.
The focused coordination typecheck and test command exits 0.
taskRails: Follow the pinned design; this task cannot create authority beyond its named contract.
Fail closed with stable codes and immutable deterministic outputs.
Keep production modules focused, target <=250 lines, split before 400.
Use TDD and stage only explicit owned paths; no worktree, broad add, push, or merge.

In one test file, enumerate every endpoint (send, read, acknowledge, replay), all five envelope kinds, and every refusal/outcome layer; assert the generated matrices are non-empty and assert exact stable code plus refusing layer. Cover exact schema/key handling, address/correlation rules, authentication and scoped capability failures, store-backed sequencing/dedupe/ack/replay, expiry, N/N+1 overload and byte/depth/count limits, unknown recipients, terminal/effect binding, response reversal, restart, and advisory/no-authority behavior. Run the focused test once and record that it is RED because the production entrypoint is absent, not because a dependency or fixture failed.

implementationPlan.description: Implement the versioned coordination contract and hostile-input codec until the contract cases turn green. Define a deeply frozen discriminated envelope union for REQUEST, RESPONSE, EVENT, CONTROL, and HANDOFF with server-owned sequence/timestamps, exact sender/recipient session addresses, mandatory correlation id, RESPONSE inReplyTo, bounded JSON data, and advisoryOnly=true for any advisory text. CONTROL is a closed non-lifecycle vocabulary; HANDOFF is structured around objective/criteria, repository/base/head/scopes, verification/artifact digests, decisions/blockers, and exact next action. Reject credential/secret and executable-command fields instead of forwarding them. Publish fixed endpoint/envelope versions, UTF-8/depth/page/TTL/outstanding-mailbox limits, and frozen result/refusal unions with stable codes and layers (DECODE, AUTHENTICATION, CAPABILITY, ADDRESS, CORRELATION, MAILBOX, STORE). Reuse the contracts bounded decoder/error vocabulary where applicable; never echo hostile bytes. Add the one-line runtime bridge.
implementationPlan.note: Implemented the versioned contract + hostile-input codec. coordination-contracts.ts publishes fixed envelope/endpoint versions, the single coordination scope, frozen sorted vocabularies (endpoints, five envelope kinds, roles, closed NON-lifecycle CONTROL kinds, seven layers, 21 stable codes), the forbidden credential/command field list, all limits (UTF-8/depth/page/TTL/outstanding-mailbox/attempts), the deeply frozen discriminated envelope union with server-owned sequence+timestamps deliberately absent from caller fields, the frozen result/refusal unions, refuse(), and coordinationCapability() as the single production source of grant strings. coordination-shape.ts holds the strict hostile-input readers (isPlainRecord rejects proxies/exotic prototypes; readOwnDataProperty rejects accessors; hasExactOwnKeys rejects extras/missing/symbols; readList indexes by readOwnDataProperty so a subclassed array, overridden Symbol.iterator, accessor element or sparse hole cannot smuggle past the length bound). coordination-parts.ts decodes addresses, advisory (advisoryOnly structurally pinned true, else COORDINATION_ADVISORY_AUTHORITY_CLAIMED), the structured HANDOFF (objective/criteria, repository/base/head/scopes, verification/artifact digests, decisions/blockers, exact nextAction), and bounded JSON data with a recursive forbidden-field scan returning COORDINATION_FORBIDDEN_FIELD instead of forwarding credential/command-shaped keys. coordination-codec.ts canonicalises to sorted-key JSON that is a pure function of caller-owned fields (so an identical resend hashes identically), digests with length-framed sha256, and re-reads the canonical bytes through the shared @moe/contracts decodeBoundedJsonBytes as an independent final gate. Refusal details name the field only and never echo hostile bytes. Added the one-line .js runtime bridges for all four modules. Evidence: focused typecheck now reports zero errors in any production module; every remaining error traces to the two not-yet-written modules (Cannot find module ./coordination-mailbox.js and ./coordination-service.js) plus the implicit-any their absence causes in the suite. Per-file physical lines: contracts 192, shape 105, parts 190, codec 235 - all under the 250 target.

implementationPlan.description: Implement the durable mailbox adapter over the public SqliteEventStore seam and drive it from the same RED suite. Persist exactly one canonical envelope event plus outbox draft atomically on a deterministic per-recipient mailbox aggregate; derive event/outbox/command identities from the bounded message id and canonical bytes. Return DEDUPLICATED only for store replay of identical bytes, map same-id/different-bytes to the exact idempotency-conflict code/layer, and propagate unknown commit ambiguity without claiming delivery. Use aggregateSequence as the mailbox cursor. Persist acknowledgements in a deterministic recipient/consumer ack aggregate, recover only its last durable event, validate monotonic ack sequence plus stored message id/digest, and make read repeat unacked entries while replay reads an explicit historical cursor without advancing it. Detect ahead/missing/non-contiguous cursors as CURSOR_GAP, calculate bounded outstanding depth for overload, and return expired messages as typed sequence-bearing EXPIRED items so callers can explicitly acknowledge them. Add bounded optimistic contention handling and the one-line runtime bridge.
implementationPlan.note: Implemented the durable mailbox over the PUBLIC SqliteEventStore seam as a structural CoordinationEventStore port (commit / getAggregateVersion / getCommandReceipt / readAggregateEvents only - no package-internal projection, relay, or SQL reach-through). coordination-mailbox-ids.ts owns the deterministic identities: mailbox aggregate per exact address (effectId participates, so a terminal wrapper and its bare session are never the same mailbox), ack aggregate derived from it, send commandId from mailbox+bounded messageId ONLY (so a resend always addresses the same durable command slot), and eventId/outboxMessageId from mailbox+messageId+canonical bytes (so identical resend collides deliberately and different bytes cannot). Server stamps (sentAt/expiresAt/digest) are stored as event METADATA, never inside the canonical bytes, so arrival time cannot perturb the digest and a later retry still deduplicates. Send: one canonical envelope event plus one outbox draft committed atomically; a pre-existing receipt whose eventIds contain the derived eventId returns DEDUPLICATED with the ORIGINAL stamps, anything else returns COORDINATION_IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT at STORE; OUTCOME_UNKNOWN maps to COORDINATION_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN and never claims delivery; EXPECTED_VERSION_CONFLICT retries under a bounded attempt cap then returns COORDINATION_STORE_BUSY. aggregateSequence is the cursor. coordination-mailbox-reads.ts recovers only the LAST durable ack event (never a full replay), reports cursor-ahead and non-contiguous sequences as typed CURSOR_GAP carrying both positions, computes bounded outstanding depth for N/N+1 overload, and returns expired entries as typed sequence-bearing EXPIRED items instead of filtering them. Acknowledge validates the stored messageId+digest at the claimed sequence first (COORDINATION_ACK_UNKNOWN_MESSAGE) then monotonicity (COORDINATION_ACK_REGRESSION), and read repeats unacked entries while replay reads an explicit historical cursor without advancing the ack. Also corrected the suite's store-failure injection: SqliteEventStore instances are Object.freeze'd so defineProperty on the instance would have thrown - failures are now injected through the structural port with every read delegated to the real store. Added the three .js bridges. Evidence: focused typecheck reports zero errors in any mailbox module; the only remaining errors are Cannot find module ./coordination-service.js and the implicit-any it causes in the suite. Per-file lines: ids 163, reads 111, mailbox 240.

implementationPlan.description: Implement the coordination service endpoints around the codec and mailbox with fail-closed dependency ports. For every send/read/acknowledge/replay request, pass the canonical request digest, endpoint kind, credential/proof presentation, transport, current time, and exact coordination scope to an injected identity authenticator; accept only a frozen positive binding whose principal/session matches the request, and keep auth material out of stored bytes. Resolve every recipient through an injected registry before storage and require exact send-kind/recipient or mailbox read/ack/replay capability. For terminal/effect-wrapper addresses, require a current positive effectId+sessionId binding; throws, UNKNOWN, stale, or mismatched answers return TERMINAL_BINDING_INVALID at ADDRESS without mailbox mutation. On RESPONSE send, load the referenced durable REQUEST and require reversed addresses and identical correlation id. Stamp time/sequence server-side, refuse already-expired sends and full mailboxes, expose no dispatch/lifecycle/effect callback, and ensure free-form advisory text remains immutable data with no authority or next-command affordance. Add the one-line runtime bridge.

Create the curated public entrypoint and finish the integration/restart cases. Export only the five envelope contracts, limits/codes/layers, dependency-port types, durable mailbox constructor, and service constructor; do not export store internals, raw SQL, credential material, or an envelope-to-command executor. Exercise the public entrypoint against a real file-backed SqliteEventStore: enqueue ordered mixed-kind messages, observe redelivery before ack, close/reopen, replay and acknowledge, reopen again, and prove the next read resumes strictly after the durable ack with identical message ids/digests/sequences. Add concurrent sends, response lookup, expiry boundary, mailbox-limit N/N+1, cursor-ahead/gap, store throw/ambiguous outcome, unknown recipient, revoked/expired/replayed auth, missing capability, and terminal-binding cases. Use mkdtemp under the OS temp directory with finally cleanup after every store close, and include a plain-Node source-entrypoint import smoke assertion so missing .js bridges cannot hide behind Vitest resolution.

Perform the single adversarial review over the owned diff before the final gate. Attack double/concurrent send and ack, replay after restart, null/array/proxy/revoked-proxy inputs, empty/negative/fractional/huge limits and TTLs, Unicode byte limits, expiry at the exact boundary, response-to-nonrequest and address swaps, recipient/effect disappearance, stale auth, store throw/OUTCOME_UNKNOWN, and advisory payloads shaped like runtime commands, shell argv, or credentials. Confirm every failure test asserts the specific code and refusing layer and every generated sweep asserts a positive case count. Mutation-drill at least authentication bypass, terminal-binding bypass, idempotency-conflict mapping, cursor-gap detection, and advisoryOnly on the production surface; each named test must go red. Restore exact owned bytes in a finally path, confirm no scratch/evidence files remain, and verify each production .ts file is at most 250 physical lines.

Run the one required foreground verification command exactly: pnpm --filter @moe/coordination typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/coordination test. Record fresh exit 0 and test counts as completion evidence. Then run git status --porcelain, ensure every staged entry is one of the ten owned packages/coordination paths and pnpm-lock.yaml is neither modified nor staged, unstage any foreign path without altering it, and commit only explicit owned pathspecs with git commit -- <owned paths>. Verify git show --stat contains only packages/coordination/** before calling moe.complete_task; do not push, merge, reset, stash, or use a broad add/commit.

comments.author: governor-c713986e
comments.content:
GOVERNOR NOTE — read this before choosing where the session coordination fabric persists its records.

task-5d79649c (Repository hygiene policy, commit 7678402) added a `.gitignore` rule for `.moe/sessions/`, classifying it as regenerable daemon scaffolding. worker-4dddabde flagged this as the one speculative entry in an otherwise evidence-backed set and asked to be second-guessed on it.

The hazard: if this fabric persists durable session records under `.moe/sessions/`, that ignore rule silently hides them. They would never be committed, and `git status` would not show them missing — the failure is invisible, which is the worst shape for a durability bug.

Two ways to clear it:
- Persist session records in the store (the epic's stated direction) rather than under `.moe/`. Then the rule is correct and nothing needs to change.
- If `.moe/sessions/` really is the right location for durable records, delete that row from `.gitignore` as part of this task and say so explicitly in the plan.

Do not leave it ambiguous. The hygiene doc carries a provisional caveat pointing whoever builds this fabric back to that row; this comment is the other half of that pointer.

Context on why the rule exists at all: the hygiene block is deliberately allow-by-omission — 12 explicitly named regenerable leaves, with anything unrecognized staying visible and defaulting to tracked. There is no blanket `.moe/` rule. So removing the `.moe/sessions/` row is a safe, local edit; it does not open a hole, it just returns that path to the visible default.

Tooling gotcha you will hit if you verify this yourself: `git check-ignore -v` exits 0 on a NEGATION match and prints the rule with a leading `!`. Branching on its exit code reports negated paths as ignored. Read the printed rule, not `$?`.

planSizeWarnings: Plan touches 10 distinct files (target <=5); plans over 10 are rejected. Small file-disjoint tasks review better and parallelize.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: Use the existing store rather than .moe/sessions or a second SQLite schema. A peer-to-peer/chat design and any envelope-to-runtime-command dispatcher are rejected because they would mint authority outside the contract. Direct imports of package-internal projection/relay/subscription modules are also rejected: coordination should consume the public @moe/store event/commit/read surface plus narrow injected identity, recipient, and effect-binding ports, while preserving the invariants established by those internal modules. Durable message and acknowledgement aggregates give strict mailbox order, store idempotency gives send dedupe, and explicit ack/replay cursors give at-least-once delivery across restart.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: The current @moe/contracts barrel exposes bounded JSON/runtime versions and stable auth/session/idempotency errors; @moe/core now re-exports its identity seam; @moe/store publicly exposes SqliteEventStore commit, aggregate/global reads, command receipts, and pending outbox pages. Store projection/outbox/subscription implementations are intentionally package-internal and establish the rules to preserve: event+outbox atomicity, inbox/message digest dedupe, strict-after cursors, typed gaps, and no silent poison skip. Persist under the store only; do not use ignored .moe/sessions. This source-consumed NodeNext workspace needs a one-line .js bridge for every non-entrypoint production .ts module. Because pnpm-lock.yaml is outside the owned paths, never stage or commit it; if workspace links must be materialized locally, use pnpm install --lockfile=false --ignore-scripts and keep the required package dependencies confined to packages/coordination/package.json.
planningNotes.risks: Authentication must bind the digest of the exact endpoint request, not trust caller-asserted sender data; auth credentials/proofs are endpoint-only and must never enter the durable envelope or logs. A RESPONSE must resolve its stored REQUEST and prove reversed addresses plus the same correlation id. Terminal/effect addresses must be positively resolved to the authenticated session and current effect binding. Reads must expose expired entries as typed sequence-bearing items rather than filter them, and an unknown/ambiguous store outcome must never become success. Bound concurrency retries, page bytes/count, TTL, outstanding depth, all strings and structured payload depth; test N and N+1. Use OS temp directories and close SQLite before cleanup for Windows/macOS/Linux. Keep each production .ts file at or below 250 physical lines.
